name: Question 3
problem: The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ about $x=0$ is
worked_solution:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!} \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡0=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡0=-1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(0) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0)$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =1+0\cdot x-1\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+0\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{6} \\  & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The third-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x)=cos⁡x about x=0 is

a
1−2x2
b
x−2x3
c
1−x2
d
x−x32
e
1−x22
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about x=0, we plug a=0 into the general formula to give P3(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)x22!+f‴(0)x33!=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)x22+f‴(0)x36.

We need to compute f(0), f′(0), f″(0), and f‴(0), as follows:

f(x)=cos⁡x⟹f(0)=cos⁡0=1f′(x)=−sin⁡x⟹f′(0)=−sin⁡0=0f″(x)=−cos⁡x⟹f″(0)=−cos⁡0=−1f‴(x)=sin⁡x⟹f‴(0)=sin⁡0=0

Finally, we plug the results for f(0), f′(0), f″(0), and f‴(0) into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives P3(x)=1+0⋅x−1⋅x22+0⋅x36=1−x22.
